//: Settings for scripts/audit-public.mjs (bun run audit:public). Its header says what each rule checks. Findings that are fine go in audit-public.allow.json; binaries are described in binary-provenance.json.
//base: The last upstream commit published under MIT, which this repository is built from. History before it is upstream's and is not read; --history <base>..HEAD and the pre-push mode start here.
//licenseBoundary: Upstream's commit that moved AgentHydra to the PolyForm Noncommercial license. No commit audited here may have it in its history. The audit and the pre-push hook have it built in, so taking it out of this file turns nothing off; a different commit id here is checked as well.
//placeholderUsers: Account names in C:\Users\<name>, /Users/<name> and /home/<name> that stand for anyone. Any other name in that place is a finding.
//commitEmails: The only addresses a commit's author, committer or trailers may carry.
//allowedEmailDomains: RFC 2606 and RFC 6761 names: an address at one of these, or at a name under one, is nobody's.
//historicalPaths: Files that record what upstream shipped; infra.host does not read them. Commit messages are treated alike for upstreamHosts, privateRepos and pathDenylist: a message that names one says what its commit takes out.
//upstreamHosts: Upstream's own services and sites. Each also matches every name under it.
//upstreamRepos: Upstream's public repository, a case-insensitive regular expression. infra.upstream-release finds its releases (github.com/<repo>/releases, /archive, /raw), its raw files (raw.githubusercontent.com/<repo>) and its GitHub API (api.github.com/repos/<repo>), the addresses an update or a download would reach upstream at, outside historicalPaths and commit messages. A link to the repository, a commit or an issue is not one. A test that names one as a case to refuse is allowed by path in audit-public.allow.json.
//privateRepos: Upstream repositories nobody outside upstream can read, and the commands only they provide. Case-insensitive regular expressions. Project Hydra and Odin are matched by their repository slugs and by their commands (ph codex, odin codex and so on), not by their bare names. Project Hydra and projecthydra name the optional connector AgentHydra has had since the base (the New screen's project source, the box doctor's checks, PROJECTHYDRA_HOME): it reaches a user's own copy and publishes nothing of upstream's, and a clone folder called project-hydra can be anyone's (upstream's own is on pathDenylist). Odin alone is a common word; most of the 49 lines that have it are upstream's run notes and chat-title fixtures.
//pathDenylist: Folders from upstream maintainers' own disks. Any spelling matches (D:/x, d:\\x).
//publicInternalHosts: Internal-looking names that are the same everywhere, so they identify no network.
//internalHostPrefixes: A .local, .lan or .home.arpa name whose first label starts like this is a placeholder.
